milestone: Brownie Runtime Release Readiness Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds a Runtime-owned explicit cancel boundary so autonomous callers can stop stale or unwanted task execution through a bounded command instead of relying on implicit terminal states.
Makes cancelled task state inspectable through durable Runtime evidence with exact replay semantics and a clear next action for task inspection.
Keeps cancellation narrowing-only and separate from completion, verification, permission grants, workspace mutation, MCP/tool authority, process control, and scheduler authority.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, progress_visualization, and runtime_permission_enforcement by adding an explicit Runtime-owned cancel command.
answers.new_capability: Callers can invoke task.cancel with authorization, task/run identity, current-state freshness, cancel_id, and receive bounded TaskCancelled evidence or an idempotent exact replay.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: TaskStatus::Cancelled and TaskCancelled events existed, but there was no public Runtime admission command that owned authorization, freshness, replay, and terminal evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could not safely expose cancellation as part of the local Runtime boundary before release; external controllers would have no bounded command contract to stop a task.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Runtime behavior by adding the cancel admission path and replay semantics, then updates VSIX validators and release-readiness guards; it is not a report-only or endpoint-count phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. RRP-2 intentionally adds the required task.cancel Runtime RPC because the release blocker is the absence of an explicit cancel command.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase does not add a diagnostic, report, digest, verdict, history, preview, or summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Created, Queued, and Running tasks can transition to Cancelled only through an authorized, fresh task.cancel request; stale, terminal, mismatched, malformed, and unauthorized requests fail closed before terminal evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless control loops can issue one bounded cancel command and safely replay the exact same cancellation without duplicate terminal events.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the explicit-cancel-command P0 blocker while Runtime Release Ready remains false until the other recorded P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decision are resolved.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-2 changes the Runtime release-readiness guard, audit, and current phase manifest. Review must confirm task.cancel is a real Runtime-owned cancel boundary, keeps CLI/VSIX thin, and does not claim Runtime Release Ready while other P0/P1 blockers remain open.

exit_criteria: Runtime exposes task.cancel as a typed JSON-RPC method.
task.cancel requires caller authorization, task/run identity, expected current status, expected task updated_at, and a bounded cancel_id.
Only Created, Queued, and Running tasks can transition to Cancelled; stale, terminal, mismatched, malformed, missing, and unauthorized requests fail closed before TaskCancelled evidence.
Exact replay is idempotent only when durable cancellation evidence matches the same cancel request fingerprint.
VSIX protocol validators and runtime client projections cover task.cancel params/results without owning cancellation policy.
Runtime Release Readiness audit marks explicit-cancel-command closed and keeps Runtime Release Ready false while remaining blockers are open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime task_cancel tests cover authorized cancellation, exact replay, stale request rejection, and terminal-task rejection without new terminal evidence.
VSIX runtimeClient tests cover task.cancel request projection plus invalid params/result rejection.
Runtime release-readiness guard requires task.cancel in the canonical Runtime boundary method subset.
Runtime release-readiness guard and phase-value guards validate the updated audit and manifest.

accepted_capability: The Runtime has an explicit, authorized, fresh, replay-safe task.cancel command.
`explicit-cancel-command` is closed as a Runtime Release Readiness P0 blocker.
behavior_evidence: Runtime tests validate successful cancel, idempotent replay, stale request fail-closed behavior, and terminal task fail-closed behavior.
VSIX tests validate task.cancel request and response shapes.
Release-readiness guard validates the canonical boundary includes task.cancel.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the cancellation, admission, replay, ledger, task lifecycle, and terminal-state authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection/validation layers.
Cancellation is narrowing-only and cannot grant completion, verification, permission, workspace mutation, MCP/tool, process-control, service-control, Mode Pack, or scheduler authority.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.

Does not add OS process-tree killing, service control, scheduler, daemon, hosted platform, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote transport, forge/notification adapters, package installation, signing infrastructure, or registry behavior.
Does not reopen MCP-S1 through MCP-S7 or RRP-1.
Does not close process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema migration, CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, or platform/deadline/durability blockers.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected treating existing Cancelled enum/event support as sufficient because it did not provide public Runtime cancel admission.
Rejected moving cancel policy into CLI or VSIX because cancellation state transitions and replay evidence are Runtime authority.
Rejected OS process-tree killing and service control because RRP-2 is the durable task cancellation contract, not process supervision.
Rejected closing recovery, migration, CI, protocol/event, decomposition, or durability blockers in this phase because each requires its own bounded evidence.
technical_debt: Remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers: real process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema version and migration, runtime-release-guard CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, runtime module decomposition reevaluation, and platform/deadline/durability hardening.
Owner license/publish decision remains required before OSS release basis can be claimed.

runtime_release_dod: Canonical Runtime boundary and VSIX validation coverage for task.cancel.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemons, hosted queues, worker fleets, leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLAs, billing, and concrete Secret Provider products.
external_adapter_responsibilities: GitHub/GitLab Apps, PR workflows, Slack/Teams/email, SIEM, OTel, customer-system adapters, remote transports, registries, package distribution, and signing infrastructure.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: After RRP-2 merge, continue to real-process-loss-recovery-e2e as the next recorded Runtime Release Readiness P0 blocker.
